scope: local-only; no AWS writes; not browser Apply/Save/Reload proof

results.summary: A coherent mobile-first nearby discovery architecture with geo indexing, cached hot queries, consent-aware friend presence, and rebuildable projections that covers the published core scope well.

findings.title: Consent-aware nearby-friends flow is well bounded
findings.explanation: The design separates friend presence from place search, requires explicit opt-in and allowed audiences, and rechecks consent at read time. This directly reduces privacy and correctness risk for nearby-friends queries.

findings.title: Search pipeline cleanly splits coarse geo filtering from exact validation
findings.explanation: Using geohash-like cells and then verifying exact distance in the service is an efficient and understandable pattern for radius queries with multiple filters.

findings.title: Rebuildable projection reduces coupling to canonical storage
findings.explanation: The search index is explicitly treated as a rebuildable projection, and the indexer consumes versioned events idempotently. This improves operability and supports safe recovery.

results.summary: The design cleanly supports nearby place and friend discovery with consent-aware presence, indexed geo filtering, caching, and rebuildable projections for large-scale mobile use.

findings.title: Mobile-first nearby discovery path is explicit
findings.explanation: The frontend is designed as a mobile app and includes OS location permission handling plus explicit nearby-friends mode, which aligns well with the target user experience.

findings.title: Combined geo-filter pipeline is well-structured
findings.explanation: The design cleanly separates candidate retrieval from exact-distance verification, while keeping category, rating, and price fields in the rebuildable projection. That supports expressive searches without forcing full scans of canonical records.

findings.title: Presence privacy is handled through consent-aware reads and expiry
findings.explanation: Friend presence is explicit opt-in, audience-scoped, expiring, and rechecked at read time, which is a strong fit for location sharing safety.

results.summary: The design coherently covers nearby place and friend search, radius-based filtering, real-time presence updates, durable reviews, and global-scale geospatial querying with a clear split between canonical storage, search indexing, and cached query paths.

findings.title: Cell-based search path matches low-latency nearby queries
findings.explanation: The design uses geospatial cells, then applies exact-distance verification in the service. That is an appropriate strategy for the required nearby search behavior without requiring a full scan of canonical records.

findings.title: Privacy-aware friend presence handling is built into the flow
findings.explanation: Opt-in presence, audience checks, versioned revocation, expiring current location, and read-time authorization are all explicitly represented across the API, cache, and event stream.

findings.title: Rebuildable projections reduce coupling between canonical data and search
findings.explanation: Canonical place and review writes go to the primary store, while the geospatial index is treated as a rebuildable projection and refreshed idempotently from events. This keeps query serving separate from durable source-of-truth writes.

results.summary: The design covers nearby place and friend discovery with radius-based search, facet filtering, consent-gated live presence, rebuildable geospatial indexing, and cache-assisted low-latency query paths.

findings.title: Clear separation between authoritative data and projections
findings.explanation: The design cleanly separates canonical place/review/consent storage from the rebuildable geospatial index and hot-query cache, which reduces coupling and supports both freshness and query speed.

findings.title: Consent-aware nearby-friends handling
findings.explanation: Friend presence is gated by explicit opt-in, allowed audience, expiry policy, and read-time consent version checks, which is well matched to the privacy-sensitive portion of the scope.

findings.title: Practical query path for radius plus facets
findings.explanation: The architecture uses cell-based retrieval for candidate reduction, then applies exact-distance verification and facet filtering, which is an appropriate pattern for low-latency location search.

results.summary: The design strongly covers nearby search, filters, reviews, mobile access, and consent-aware friend presence, with good use of geospatial indexing and cache/projection layers. Remaining gaps are mostly around explicit global-routing, failure fallback, operational visibility, and implementation-ready degraded-mode behavior.

findings.title: Global scale strategy is directionally sound but not fully specified
findings.explanation: The design shows geographic sharding, cross-region replication, and rebuildable projections, which are appropriate for millions of users and places. However, it does not spell out cross-region request routing or how query ownership is selected globally, so the scale story remains slightly underdefined for worldwide traffic distribution.
findings.recommendation: Add a brief global-routing strategy, such as region affinity with nearest-region reads and controlled replication/failover for writes.

findings.title: Failure handling for location freshness is partially implicit
findings.explanation: The architecture uses expiring presence, versioned updates, and idempotent consumers, which helps reliability. But the response path relies on freshness metadata and asynchronous projection updates without an explicit fallback for stale or missing presence state, so the user-visible behavior during propagation delays is not fully defined.
findings.recommendation: Specify the read-path fallback when presence or projection freshness is degraded, such as returning stale-labeled results, retrying from canonical state, or suppressing friend visibility until revalidated.

findings.title: Authorization model for friend presence could use tighter read-path detail
findings.explanation: The system includes JWT authentication, audience authorization, consent-version revocation, and opt-in gating, which is strong. The remaining ambiguity is the exact enforcement point for friend-result reads when cache or index entries are stale; that is a clarification issue rather than a missing control.
findings.recommendation: Clarify whether every friend-location read is reauthorized against canonical consent before returning cached or projected results.

findings.title: Query path is well-designed but exact latency behavior is unproven
findings.explanation: The design has the right performance primitives for low-latency geo queries: bounded candidate retrieval, cache-aside hot queries, and exact-distance verification outside the index. Still, the system does not specify cache hit expectations, index fanout bounds, or any load-shedding strategy for very hot regions, so performance under bursty demand remains partly unspecified.
findings.recommendation: Add a brief hot-path policy for cache use, candidate limits, and degradation behavior when the query rate spikes in a dense region.

findings.title: Operational visibility is present but not comprehensive
findings.explanation: The design exposes projection freshness metadata and consumer lag, which is a useful observability baseline. However, it does not explicitly surface request-level metrics or alerting hooks for stale presence, cache invalidation delays, or geo-index rebuild failure, leaving some important operational failure modes only partially observable.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit metrics/alerts for query latency, cache hit rate, presence staleness, index rebuild lag, and consumer failure rate.

findings.title: Implementation detail is sufficient, but a few policy choices remain open
findings.explanation: The design gives concrete roles, data flows, and update semantics, so it is implementable at a high level. The only open pieces are freshness windows and the exact cache invalidation policy, which are tractable product/operations decisions rather than blocking gaps.
findings.recommendation: Document the freshness policy and invalidation thresholds for cached place results and presence entries.

findings.title: Request routing and service responsibilities are clearly separated
findings.explanation: The gateway authenticates and validates, the backend applies query and consent logic, the index handles spatial retrieval, and workers handle refresh/projection. This separation makes the design easy to reason about and matches the mobile-first and geo-query scope well.

findings.title: Cost profile is reasonable but not explicitly bounded
findings.explanation: Using rebuildable projections, cache-aside hot queries, and bounded geospatial candidate retrieval is cost-conscious for a high-query-volume service. The remaining cost uncertainty is the operational expense of cross-region replication and dual storage of projections versus canonical data, which is not justified with workload assumptions.
findings.recommendation: State the intended read/write mix or region footprint assumptions, and note which replicas or caches can be scaled down during low demand.

findings.title: Most core behaviors are covered, with one scope nuance around friend results
findings.explanation: The architecture addresses nearby place search, filters, reviews, mobile access, and real-time updates. The friend-presence path is present, but its read-time policy depends on freshness and authorization checks that are split across layers, so the core behavior is covered with some operational nuance.
findings.recommendation: Keep the friend-results path explicitly documented as a consent-checked, freshness-labeled read flow.

findings.title: Constraint compliance is strong, but global scale could be stated more concretely
findings.explanation: The design meets the key constraints with geospatial indexing, low-latency query paths, and frequent-update handling. The only remaining issue is that global scale is implied through geographic sharding and cross-region replication rather than fully spelled out as an end-to-end traffic placement strategy.
findings.recommendation: Describe the region-selection policy for reads and how writes or updates propagate between regions.

findings.title: Component responsibilities are coherent and well-justified
findings.explanation: Each major component has a clear purpose: mobile client, gateway, backend service, canonical store, search index, cache, broker, and workers. The indexing and cache choices are particularly well aligned with the location-query workload and update patterns.

findings.title: Connection semantics are mostly clear but hot-path degradation is not described
findings.explanation: The connections include direction, protocol, and purpose, which makes the data flow understandable. What is still unclear is how the service behaves if the geospatial index, event stream, or cache is temporarily unavailable during a query burst.
findings.recommendation: Add fallback behavior for index/cache unavailability, such as degraded results, retries, or temporary suppression of friend presence reads.

findings.title: Implementation handoff details are sufficient for core flows
findings.explanation: The architecture includes concrete components, data stores, projections, and message flow for the core feature set, so a team could start implementation from it. It still needs explicit policy decisions for freshness and regional routing, but those are refinement items rather than blockers.

findings.title: Missing explicit implementation readiness for query-response degradation
findings.explanation: The design does not specify the exact API behavior when the geo index or cache is partially unavailable, which affects whether the system can be handed off without ambiguity for the hot query path.
findings.recommendation: Document whether the service should fail open with stale data, fail closed, or return partial results under component degradation.

results.summary: The design is well-scoped for Google Calendar core behavior, with solid support for CRUD, recurrence, sharing, reminders, availability, multi-device sync, and concurrency-safe updates.

findings.title: No material core gaps detected
findings.explanation: The submitted architecture covers event CRUD, recurrence, sharing, invitations/reminders, availability, multi-calendar membership, scale-out storage, device sync, concurrent edit handling, timezone-aware recurrence, real-time notification delivery, conflict detection, and consistency mechanisms.

results.summary: The design covers event CRUD, recurrence, sharing, invitations, availability, multi-calendar support, scaling, and device sync with coherent revisioned and ACL-aware flows.

findings.title: Revision-checked writes prevent lost updates
findings.explanation: The API explicitly requires a base revision and returns a conflict instead of overwriting concurrent edits, which directly addresses the same-event update constraint.

findings.title: Timezone-aware recurrence expansion is well scoped
findings.explanation: Recurring events are expanded using local wall-clock rules plus IANA timezones and a declared DST policy, which preserves meeting intent across timezone changes.

findings.title: Sync pipeline supports device consistency
findings.explanation: The delta sync service, tombstones, and cursor-based replay provide a coherent cross-device synchronization model with explicit conflict handling.

results.summary: The design covers the legacy calendar scope with transactional event edits, ACL-based sharing, recurrence expansion, conflict-aware availability, durable reminders, and cursor-based cross-device sync.

findings.title: Revision-aware mutation path prevents lost updates
findings.explanation: Event writes require a stable idempotency key and a base-event revision, and conflicting concurrent edits are returned explicitly instead of overwriting each other.

findings.title: Timezone-safe recurrence expansion is explicitly modeled
findings.explanation: Recurring events are expanded from local wall-clock rules with IANA timezone data and DST policy, which preserves meeting intent across daylight-saving transitions.

findings.title: Sync and notification paths are durable and revalidated
findings.explanation: The design uses revisioned delta sync, tombstones, durable outbox/broker delivery, and notification rechecks before sending, which reduces duplicate or stale user-facing actions.

results.summary: The design covers the published calendar scope well: CRUD, recurring events, sharing, invitations, availability, multi-calendar support, and cross-device sync are all mapped to coherent services with revision-based conflict handling and timezone-aware recurrence.

findings.title: Revision-aware writes prevent lost updates
findings.explanation: The command API requires a stable base revision and returns an explicit conflict rather than overwriting concurrent edits. This directly addresses same-event concurrent modification without long-lived locks.

findings.title: Timezone and DST handling are modeled explicitly
findings.explanation: Recurring expansion uses an IANA timezone, local recurrence rules, and an explicit DST gap/overlap policy, which is the right model for preserving meeting intent across timezone changes.

findings.title: Availability queries are freshness-aware and ACL-safe
findings.explanation: The availability path bounds queries, checks current ACL/privacy rules, and marks results with an as-of watermark so stale free/busy data is not treated as authoritative.

results.summary: Strong calendar core coverage is present, including CRUD, recurrence, sharing, reminders, sync, and conflict-aware updates; the main gap is that availability is only advisory and the design does not show an enforced scheduling decision path.

findings.title: Availability is advisory, but no enforced scheduling path is shown
findings.explanation: The design provides availability queries and overlap detection, yet the Availability + Conflict Service explicitly says free/busy is advisory unless a separate reservation transaction exists. No such reservation component or connection is defined, so the architecture does not clearly show how a client turns an availability result into a conflict-free scheduling decision for event creation.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit scheduling/reservation decision path in the Calendar API that checks current busy state and either commits the event atomically or returns a conflict when the slot is no longer available.

results.summary: The design cleanly covers publishing, routing, durable persistence, retries, dead-letter handling, ordering, pub/sub, point-to-point delivery, and priority work with a coherent broker-centered flow.

findings.title: Durable broker confirmation and retry isolation are well aligned with reliability goals
findings.explanation: The architecture confirms publishes only after durable quorum commit, keeps retry state durable, and isolates terminal failures in a dead-letter queue. That combination directly supports no-loss handling and consumer-failure recovery.

findings.title: Per-key ordering is preserved across the main delivery paths
findings.explanation: The broker preserves per-key order, the point-to-point queue retains a key behind an uncompleted head during retry, and retry scheduling rechecks ordering before release. This is a coherent ordering story across normal delivery and recovery.

results.summary: The design cleanly covers publish/consume, durable multi-queue routing, ordering, retries, dead-letter handling, and priority work dispatch with a coherent replicated broker and consumer-group flow.

findings.title: Durable broker confirmation and retry isolation form a strong reliability path
findings.explanation: The broker only confirms after a durable quorum commit, consumers acknowledge after committed effects, and failed deliveries are persisted to retry or dead-letter queues. This directly supports reliable asynchronous communication with consumer-failure recovery.

findings.title: Ordering is preserved across normal delivery and retry flows
findings.explanation: Per-key ordering is maintained in the broker, topic backlogs, point-to-point queue, and retry scheduling, so retries do not break the stated ordering guarantee.

findings.title: Priority work queue addresses the stated priority-queue constraint
findings.explanation: The point-to-point queue explicitly schedules priority among eligible heads for different keys, which satisfies the priority-queue constraint without adding a separate subsystem.

results.summary: A coherent durable queue architecture with replicated broker storage, topic fan-out, competing-consumer work queues, retry handling, and dead-letter isolation that matches the published core scope.

findings.title: Replicated broker and durable queues cover the core reliability path
findings.explanation: The design consistently routes publishes through a replicated broker, durable subscription backlogs, durable retry storage, and a dead-letter queue, which gives a coherent path for persistence, retries, and terminal failure handling.

findings.title: Priority and ordering are integrated into the work-queue model
findings.explanation: The point-to-point queue explicitly combines priority scheduling with FIFO ordering within each ordering key, which is a strong fit for the stated priority-queue constraint without sacrificing per-key ordering.

results.summary: The design presents a coherent RabbitMQ-like distributed queue with durable replication, pub/sub and point-to-point delivery, ordered retries, and dead-letter isolation, matching the published core scope.

findings.title: Durable brokered queue architecture covers the core RabbitMQ-like workflow
findings.explanation: The design coherently connects producers, a replicated durable broker, topic subscription queues, point-to-point queues, consumer groups, retry handling, and dead-letter isolation. The resulting flow supports publish/consume, pub/sub and point-to-point delivery, acknowledgments, retries, ordering, and failure recovery without requiring extra infrastructure beyond the stated scope.

findings.title: Workload-tuned partitioning and bounded in-flight work support scale and latency
findings.explanation: The broker uses durable replicated partition logs and bounded flow control, while consumer groups process assigned partitions with bounded prefetch and in-flight work. That is a credible strategy for the stated high throughput and low latency goals.

findings.title: Retry and dead-letter handling preserve failure isolation without losing ordering context
findings.explanation: Retry envelopes carry original IDs, sequence numbers, ordering keys, attempt history, and due times, and terminal failures are retained in a dead-letter queue. This supports consumer failure handling while preserving the information needed for controlled redrive or inspection.

results.summary: A coherent distributed-queue design with durable publish/ack semantics, partitioned topic fan-out, point-to-point competing consumers, ordered retries, and dead-letter handling; it covers the published core scope without material gaps.

findings.title: Durable broker commit before accept strengthens loss prevention
findings.explanation: The producer path treats only a durable broker confirmation as accepted, and the broker confirms only after quorum-durable replication. That directly supports the no-loss and durability goals.

findings.title: Explicit retry and dead-letter lifecycle covers failure handling
findings.explanation: The design separates transient retry from terminal dead-letter storage, preserving message identity, ordering context, and attempt history. This is a strong fit for consumer failure recovery and failure isolation.

results.summary: A coherent hotel booking architecture with authoritative inventory ownership, retry-safe booking/payment flows, cache-assisted search, and event-driven invalidation and notifications.

findings.title: Authoritative inventory ownership is clearly separated from read accelerators
findings.explanation: The design keeps the Booking and Inventory Service and its store as the source of truth, while the search index and cache are explicitly treated as non-authoritative accelerators. This is a strong pattern for avoiding stale inventory decisions.

findings.title: Idempotency and transactional outbox improve booking correctness
findings.explanation: The gateway deduplicates retrying clients, the booking store persists idempotency records, and the transactional outbox feeds events to downstream consumers. Together these decisions materially reduce duplicate reservation side effects and make asynchronous notifications safer.

findings.title: Clear separation between synchronous commands and asynchronous side effects
findings.explanation: The design routes booking and cancellation commands synchronously to the inventory owner, then uses events for cache invalidation, search refresh, and notifications. This keeps core reservation state changes direct while allowing non-critical side effects to lag safely.

results.summary: The design cleanly separates search, authoritative inventory, and payment handling, with transactional booking state, idempotency, and event-driven cache/notification updates supporting the core hotel reservation workflow.

findings.title: Durable reservation and inventory ownership
findings.explanation: The design centralizes reservation state in the Booking and Inventory Service and persists authoritative state in the booking store, which is the right pattern for preventing stale reads from authorizing a booking.

findings.title: Idempotent payment and retry handling
findings.explanation: The API gateway deduplicates client retries and the payment flow uses a durable operation identity, which reduces duplicate booking attempts and duplicate charge risk.

findings.title: Cache invalidation tied to committed inventory changes
findings.explanation: The availability cache is explicitly treated as provisional and is refreshed or invalidated from committed booking events, which preserves correctness while still allowing read acceleration.

findings.title: Asynchronous notifications are separated from transactional booking flow
findings.explanation: Confirmation, cancellation, and refund messages are emitted after committed booking events, avoiding coupling guest messaging to the reservation transaction path.

results.summary: The design covers hotel search, real-time availability, booking and cancellation, concurrency control, payment confirmation, inventory ownership, and post-commit cache/search updates with a coherent transactional flow.

findings.title: Clear separation between search, inventory ownership, and payment handling
findings.explanation: The design cleanly separates candidate search, authoritative inventory checks, reservation state management, and payment processing, which reduces coupling and supports the core hotel-booking workflow.

findings.title: Idempotency and transactional outbox improve retry safety
findings.explanation: The API Gateway deduplicates retrying clients, the booking store persists idempotency records, and the transactional outbox feeds durable events to downstream consumers. This is a strong fit for concurrent booking requests and asynchronous notification/update flows.

results.summary: A coherent hotel booking architecture with authoritative inventory ownership, idempotent booking/payment flows, and event-driven availability updates that covers the published core scope.

findings.title: Transactional booking ownership prevents inventory conflicts
findings.explanation: The inventory-owning booking service plus authoritative OLTP store is the right control point for holds, confirmations, cancellations, and release, which directly addresses reservation correctness under concurrent requests.

findings.title: Event-driven invalidation keeps derived views fresh
findings.explanation: Committed inventory-change events update the availability cache and search projections, which is a coherent way to preserve real-time-ish reads without making derived data authoritative.

findings.title: Idempotency support reduces retry-related booking risk
findings.explanation: The gateway deduplicates client retries and the payment flow uses durable reservation identity, which strengthens correctness for repeated booking or payment attempts.

results.summary: The design cleanly covers hotel search, real-time availability, reservation lifecycle, payment reconciliation, inventory authority, and cancellation/refund flows with coherent components and connections.

findings.title: Authoritative inventory ownership is well-defined
findings.explanation: The design cleanly separates search projections from sellable inventory. Reservation authority stays in the Booking and Inventory Service and the booking store, which is the right control for preventing oversell and keeping search responses provisional.

findings.title: Idempotent payment and booking state flow
findings.explanation: The booking service links payment attempts to a durable reservation identity and receives payment results back for confirmation or reconciliation. That is a strong pattern for avoiding duplicate charges and handling uncertain payment outcomes.

results.summary: The design covers the core A/B testing lifecycle, sticky assignment, event collection, statistical analysis, concurrent experiments, targeting, high-volume processing, live monitoring, and gradual rollout with a coherent service split.

findings.title: Versioned assignment and outbox provide a strong consistency boundary
findings.explanation: The assignment service writes to the ledger atomically and preserves the first assignment per user and experiment, which supports sticky assignment and reliable downstream delivery without relying on cache correctness.

findings.title: End-to-end analytics path is well-formed for live and historical results
findings.explanation: The design cleanly separates event validation/aggregation, durable analytics storage, and statistical analysis, which supports both real-time monitoring and reproducible post-hoc analysis.

findings.title: Experiment targeting and rollout responsibilities are clearly separated
findings.explanation: The registry owns versioned configuration and segment references, while the rollout provider and assignment service consume that configuration to decide eligibility and variant assignment. This keeps targeting, rollout, and assignment responsibilities understandable.

results.summary: The design broadly covers experiment creation, deterministic assignment, event collection, statistical analysis, concurrent experiments, segmentation, and live monitoring, with two main gaps around client event delivery guarantees and rollout-source-of-truth clarity.

findings.title: Client-side event delivery guarantees are not fully specified
findings.explanation: The client SDK emits exposure and outcome events, and the event API/broker path is durable once events reach the boundary, but the design does not specify how the SDK retries, buffers offline, or confirms delivery back to the caller. That leaves a gap for lost exposure/outcome events under transient network failure, which can undercount metrics.
findings.recommendation: Specify client acknowledgement and retry semantics, or make the SDK clearly queue-and-flush events with bounded retry and deduplication identifiers.

findings.title: The rollout-source-of-truth relationship is ambiguous
findings.explanation: Both the registry and the feature-flag provider feed assignment, but the design does not clearly state which source is authoritative when rollout state and experiment configuration diverge. This makes the assignment path harder to reason about during phased rollouts and can produce inconsistent eligibility decisions.
findings.recommendation: Define a single authoritative source for rollout eligibility and versioning, and document how registry updates propagate to the flag provider and assignment service.

findings.title: Live operational visibility is a clear strength
findings.explanation: The monitor exposes assignment errors, freshness, lag, per-variant counts, and sample-ratio diagnostics, which directly supports real-time experiment monitoring and bias detection.

findings.title: Durable assignment ledger improves consistency
findings.explanation: Persisting each assignment with its configuration version and using the ledger as authoritative after cache misses supports sticky assignment and reproducible analysis.

results.summary: Coherent A/B testing platform with versioned experiment management, deterministic assignment, durable event capture, statistical analysis, and live monitoring aligned to the published core scope.

findings.title: Deterministic assignment and durable stickiness are well aligned with core experiment semantics
findings.explanation: The design combines experiment-scoped targeting, authoritative ledger persistence, and a cache that can be rebuilt from durable state, which is a strong fit for consistent per-user assignment and repeat lookups.

findings.title: Event pipeline supports both operational monitoring and historical analysis
findings.explanation: The broker, stream validation, analytics store, and live monitor create a coherent path from ingestion to rolling metrics and backfilled analysis, which matches the need for real-time monitoring and reproducible results.

findings.title: Versioned registry cleanly centralizes experiment configuration
findings.explanation: Experiment definitions, segment references, allocation rules, and metric plans are kept in one versioned registry and propagated to assignment and analytics consumers, reducing configuration drift.

results.summary: The design covers experiment creation, deterministic assignment, event capture, statistical analysis, concurrent experiments, targeting, rollout support, and live monitoring with a coherent control-plane and data-plane split.

findings.title: Coherent end-to-end experiment lifecycle
findings.explanation: The design cleanly separates experiment definition, assignment, event capture, aggregation, and analysis, which makes the core A/B testing workflow understandable and implementable.

findings.title: High-volume processing path is well chosen
findings.explanation: The broker plus continuous stream processor and warehouse create a sensible path for billions of events and concurrent experiments without forcing synchronous analytics.

results.summary: The design covers experiment creation, deterministic assignment, event ingestion, statistical analysis, concurrent experiments, segmentation, gradual rollouts, and live monitoring with a coherent control-plane and data-plane split.

findings.title: Deterministic sticky assignment and durable ledgering support experiment correctness
findings.explanation: The design preserves first assignment per user and experiment, and persists the assignment with configuration version plus an outbox record. That combination supports consistent variant assignment and downstream correlation after retries or cache misses.

findings.title: End-to-end live monitoring is explicitly modeled
findings.explanation: The live monitor surfaces assignment errors, event freshness, processing lag, per-variant counts, and sample-ratio diagnostics, which is strong operational coverage for a testing platform.

results.summary: The design cleanly separates authoritative like membership from derived count projections, and it uses sharding, outbox delivery, and reconciliation to support viral-scale real-time like counting with privacy-aware liker reads.

findings.title: Sharded write and count path for viral posts
findings.explanation: The design uses hash-based membership buckets, a replayable stream, and sharded counter aggregation, which is a strong match for high fan-in posts and billions of likes per day.

findings.title: Separation of authoritative membership from derived counts
findings.explanation: Exact liked state is kept in the membership store while counts are maintained in rebuildable rollups and cache, which reduces ambiguity between correctness and read latency.

findings.title: Privacy-aware liker reads and live fan-out
findings.explanation: The read path explicitly gates liker-list access and live count delivery on visibility and viewer policy, which is appropriate for exposing who liked a post without over-broad disclosure.

findings.title: Idempotent mutation handling
findings.explanation: The gateway validates idempotency keys and deduplicates safe retries, while the membership store enforces conditional uniqueness, which is a robust pattern for like/unlike commands.

results.summary: The design maps the like workflow to an exact-membership source of truth, sharded transition processing, derived count rollups, and reconciliation, covering real-time counts, unlike support, duplicate prevention, privacy-filtered liker reads, and viral-post scale.

findings.title: Separation of exact membership from derived counts is well designed
findings.explanation: The architecture cleanly isolates authoritative like state from aggregate count projections, which reduces contention and makes viral-post scaling more manageable while preserving accuracy through reconciliation.

findings.title: Idempotent write and replay path reduces duplicate side effects
findings.explanation: The gateway, outbox relay, event stream, and counter worker all include deduplication and unique transition IDs, which is a strong fit for retry-heavy like operations.

findings.title: Privacy-aware liker list access is explicitly modeled
findings.explanation: The design does not expose liker identities broadly; it gates list reads through auth and visibility/block checks, which is appropriate for the 'show who liked the post' requirement.

results.summary: The design satisfies the core like-counting scope with an exact membership source, shard-aware async counting, privacy-gated liker reads, and reconciliation for count accuracy under viral load.

findings.title: End-to-end like pipeline is well decomposed
findings.explanation: The design cleanly separates command validation, identity, exact membership, durable transition relay, aggregation, cache serving, fan-out, and reconciliation. This supports the core like-counting workload without collapsing read and write concerns into one hot path.

findings.title: High-volume count path is shard-aware and replayable
findings.explanation: Viral-post writes are distributed by shard, transitions are durable and uniquely identified, and the aggregation layer can rebuild from rollups and reconciliation. That is a strong fit for the stated scale and eventual-consistency model.

results.summary: The design cleanly separates authoritative like membership from derived count projections, using sharded write paths, durable eventing, and reconciliation to support viral-scale real-time likes and liker-list reads.

findings.title: Sharded, replayable pipeline fits viral like volume
findings.explanation: The design decomposes the like pipeline into exact membership writes, durable outbox publication, partitioned event streaming, sharded aggregation, and cached reads. That provides a coherent capacity strategy for viral posts and high daily volume without relying on a single counter bottleneck.

findings.title: Exact membership plus reconciliation supports correctness for toggles and duplicate prevention
findings.explanation: The system keeps authoritative like state in the exact membership store, applies desired-state like/unlike commands, and uses reconciliation to repair derived counts from the authoritative source. This is a strong fit for undo/unlike and duplicate suppression.

findings.title: Privacy-aware liker list access is represented end to end
findings.explanation: The API paginates liker identities only after visibility and block-policy checks, and the client requests privacy-authorized pages of liker identities. That directly covers the 'show who liked the post' requirement without exposing raw membership data broadly.

results.summary: The design uses an authoritative membership store, asynchronous derived counters, reconciliation, and authorized live fan-out to cover real-time likes, unlike handling, duplicate prevention, and hot-post scaling.

findings.title: Sharded exact-membership and derived-count split is well aligned with hot-post scale
findings.explanation: The design cleanly separates authoritative membership from derived count projections, which is a strong fit for viral posts and high write volume while preserving recoverability.

findings.title: Real-time visible count updates are supported through cache plus fan-out
findings.explanation: The architecture provides both a fast read path for counts and a live update path for active viewers, so the UI can reflect changes without waiting for recomputation on every request.

results.summary: The design covers login, registration, sessions, MFA, reset, OAuth/social login, rate limiting, and large-scale operation with coherent security controls; the main open point is a fully explicit GDPR compliance story.

findings.title: Privacy and GDPR posture is described, but not fully asserted
findings.explanation: The architecture includes minimized data collection, pseudonymous audit records, and legal-review-based retention, which are good privacy controls. However, it does not explicitly state the full GDPR operating model for subject rights, lawful basis, and deletion/retention handling across all data stores.
findings.recommendation: Clarify the GDPR compliance approach for identity, audit, backup, and recovery data, including subject access/correction/deletion workflows and the legal basis for retention.

findings.title: Password upgrade path is well-defined
findings.explanation: The design correctly supports legacy bcrypt verification and upgrades successful logins to Argon2id, which gives a safe migration path without recovering plaintext passwords.

findings.title: Session revocation is centralized and immediate
findings.explanation: Using opaque session credentials resolved through Redis allows logout, reset, MFA recovery, and security actions to revoke sessions consistently across service instances.

findings.title: OAuth flow is defended against replay and unsafe linking
findings.explanation: The service validates allow-listed redirects, one-time state, nonce, PKCE, issuer, and audience, and it performs server-side code exchange. This is a strong OAuth/OIDC implementation pattern for the stated scope.

results.summary: The design strongly covers login, password security, sessions, MFA, reset, OAuth/OIDC, rate limiting, and low-latency scaling; the main unresolved gap is that GDPR/privacy compliance is described only at a high level rather than as a complete operating model.

findings.title: GDPR/privacy compliance is not fully specified
findings.explanation: The architecture shows privacy-oriented minimization and reviewed retention, but it does not define the operational GDPR mechanisms needed to demonstrate compliance end to end, such as lawful basis handling, subject-access/correction/deletion workflows, or how deletion propagates to backups and linked security records.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit GDPR workflows and ownership for data subject requests, retention/deletion enforcement, backup deletion policy, and legal-basis handling for identity, audit, and recovery data.

results.summary: The design provides a coherent, security-focused authentication architecture with strong coverage for registration, login, session revocation, MFA, password reset, OAuth/OIDC, abuse controls, and privacy-aware data handling.

findings.title: Opaque server-side sessions are a strong fit for revocation-heavy authentication

findings.title: Rate limiting is distributed and abuse-aware
findings.explanation: The limiter shares per-IP and per-account counters across instances and avoids revealing account existence, which directly supports brute-force resistance at the edge of the authentication flow.

results.summary: A coherent mobile-first nearby discovery architecture with geo indexing, cached hot queries, consent-aware friend presence, and rebuildable projections that covers the published core scope well.

findings.title: Consent-aware nearby-friends flow is well bounded
findings.explanation: The design separates friend presence from place search, requires explicit opt-in and allowed audiences, and rechecks consent at read time. This directly reduces privacy and correctness risk for nearby-friends queries.

findings.title: Search pipeline cleanly splits coarse geo filtering from exact validation
findings.explanation: Using geohash-like cells and then verifying exact distance in the service is an efficient and understandable pattern for radius queries with multiple filters.

findings.title: Rebuildable projection reduces coupling to canonical storage
findings.explanation: The search index is explicitly treated as a rebuildable projection, and the indexer consumes versioned events idempotently. This improves operability and supports safe recovery.

results.summary: A coherent hotel booking architecture with authoritative inventory ownership, retry-safe booking/payment flows, cache-assisted search, and event-driven invalidation and notifications.

findings.title: Authoritative inventory ownership is clearly separated from read accelerators
findings.explanation: The design keeps the Booking and Inventory Service and its store as the source of truth, while the search index and cache are explicitly treated as non-authoritative accelerators. This is a strong pattern for avoiding stale inventory decisions.

findings.title: Idempotency and transactional outbox improve booking correctness
findings.explanation: The gateway deduplicates retrying clients, the booking store persists idempotency records, and the transactional outbox feeds events to downstream consumers. Together these decisions materially reduce duplicate reservation side effects and make asynchronous notifications safer.

findings.title: Clear separation between synchronous commands and asynchronous side effects
findings.explanation: The design routes booking and cancellation commands synchronously to the inventory owner, then uses events for cache invalidation, search refresh, and notifications. This keeps core reservation state changes direct while allowing non-critical side effects to lag safely.

results.summary: The design cleanly covers publishing, routing, durable persistence, retries, dead-letter handling, ordering, pub/sub, point-to-point delivery, and priority work with a coherent broker-centered flow.

findings.title: Durable broker confirmation and retry isolation are well aligned with reliability goals
findings.explanation: The architecture confirms publishes only after durable quorum commit, keeps retry state durable, and isolates terminal failures in a dead-letter queue. That combination directly supports no-loss handling and consumer-failure recovery.

findings.title: Per-key ordering is preserved across the main delivery paths
findings.explanation: The broker preserves per-key order, the point-to-point queue retains a key behind an uncompleted head during retry, and retry scheduling rechecks ordering before release. This is a coherent ordering story across normal delivery and recovery.

results.summary: The design covers the core A/B testing lifecycle, sticky assignment, event collection, statistical analysis, concurrent experiments, targeting, high-volume processing, live monitoring, and gradual rollout with a coherent service split.

findings.title: Versioned assignment and outbox provide a strong consistency boundary
findings.explanation: The assignment service writes to the ledger atomically and preserves the first assignment per user and experiment, which supports sticky assignment and reliable downstream delivery without relying on cache correctness.

findings.title: End-to-end analytics path is well-formed for live and historical results
findings.explanation: The design cleanly separates event validation/aggregation, durable analytics storage, and statistical analysis, which supports both real-time monitoring and reproducible post-hoc analysis.

findings.title: Experiment targeting and rollout responsibilities are clearly separated
findings.explanation: The registry owns versioned configuration and segment references, while the rollout provider and assignment service consume that configuration to decide eligibility and variant assignment. This keeps targeting, rollout, and assignment responsibilities understandable.

results.summary: The design cleanly separates authoritative like membership from derived count projections, and it uses sharding, outbox delivery, and reconciliation to support viral-scale real-time like counting with privacy-aware liker reads.

findings.title: Sharded write and count path for viral posts
findings.explanation: The design uses hash-based membership buckets, a replayable stream, and sharded counter aggregation, which is a strong match for high fan-in posts and billions of likes per day.

findings.title: Separation of authoritative membership from derived counts
findings.explanation: Exact liked state is kept in the membership store while counts are maintained in rebuildable rollups and cache, which reduces ambiguity between correctness and read latency.

findings.title: Privacy-aware liker reads and live fan-out
findings.explanation: The read path explicitly gates liker-list access and live count delivery on visibility and viewer policy, which is appropriate for exposing who liked a post without over-broad disclosure.

findings.title: Idempotent mutation handling
findings.explanation: The gateway validates idempotency keys and deduplicates safe retries, while the membership store enforces conditional uniqueness, which is a robust pattern for like/unlike commands.

findings.explanation: The broker only confirms after a durable quorum commit, consumers acknowledge after committed effects, and failed deliveries are persisted to retry or dead-letter queues. This directly supports reliable asynchronous communication with consumer-failure recovery.

findings.title: Priority work queue addresses the stated priority-queue constraint

findings.title: Revision-checked writes prevent lost updates
findings.explanation: The API explicitly requires a base revision and returns a conflict instead of overwriting concurrent edits, which directly addresses the same-event update constraint.

findings.title: Timezone-aware recurrence expansion is well scoped

findings.title: Sync pipeline supports device consistency

results.summary: The design cleanly separates search, authoritative inventory, and payment handling, with transactional booking state, idempotency, and event-driven cache/notification updates supporting the core hotel reservation workflow.

findings.title: Durable reservation and inventory ownership
findings.explanation: The design centralizes reservation state in the Booking and Inventory Service and persists authoritative state in the booking store, which is the right pattern for preventing stale reads from authorizing a booking.

findings.title: Idempotent payment and retry handling
findings.explanation: The API gateway deduplicates client retries and the payment flow uses a durable operation identity, which reduces duplicate booking attempts and duplicate charge risk.

findings.title: Cache invalidation tied to committed inventory changes
findings.explanation: The availability cache is explicitly treated as provisional and is refreshed or invalidated from committed booking events, which preserves correctness while still allowing read acceleration.

findings.title: Asynchronous notifications are separated from transactional booking flow
findings.explanation: Confirmation, cancellation, and refund messages are emitted after committed booking events, avoiding coupling guest messaging to the reservation transaction path.

findings.title: Mobile-first nearby discovery path is explicit

findings.title: Combined geo-filter pipeline is well-structured
findings.explanation: The design cleanly separates candidate retrieval from exact-distance verification, while keeping category, rating, and price fields in the rebuildable projection. That supports expressive searches without forcing full scans of canonical records.

findings.title: Presence privacy is handled through consent-aware reads and expiry
findings.explanation: Friend presence is explicit opt-in, audience-scoped, expiring, and rechecked at read time, which is a strong fit for location sharing safety.

results.summary: The design maps the like workflow to an exact-membership source of truth, sharded transition processing, derived count rollups, and reconciliation, covering real-time counts, unlike support, duplicate prevention, privacy-filtered liker reads, and viral-post scale.

results.summary: The design broadly covers experiment creation, deterministic assignment, event collection, statistical analysis, concurrent experiments, segmentation, and live monitoring, with two main gaps around client event delivery guarantees and rollout-source-of-truth clarity.

findings.title: Client-side event delivery guarantees are not fully specified
findings.explanation: The client SDK emits exposure and outcome events, and the event API/broker path is durable once events reach the boundary, but the design does not specify how the SDK retries, buffers offline, or confirms delivery back to the caller. That leaves a gap for lost exposure/outcome events under transient network failure, which can undercount metrics.
findings.recommendation: Specify client acknowledgement and retry semantics, or make the SDK clearly queue-and-flush events with bounded retry and deduplication identifiers.

findings.title: The rollout-source-of-truth relationship is ambiguous
findings.explanation: Both the registry and the feature-flag provider feed assignment, but the design does not clearly state which source is authoritative when rollout state and experiment configuration diverge. This makes the assignment path harder to reason about during phased rollouts and can produce inconsistent eligibility decisions.
findings.recommendation: Define a single authoritative source for rollout eligibility and versioning, and document how registry updates propagate to the flag provider and assignment service.

findings.title: Live operational visibility is a clear strength
findings.explanation: The monitor exposes assignment errors, freshness, lag, per-variant counts, and sample-ratio diagnostics, which directly supports real-time experiment monitoring and bias detection.

findings.title: Durable assignment ledger improves consistency
findings.explanation: Persisting each assignment with its configuration version and using the ledger as authoritative after cache misses supports sticky assignment and reproducible analysis.

results.summary: A coherent durable queue architecture with replicated broker storage, topic fan-out, competing-consumer work queues, retry handling, and dead-letter isolation that matches the published core scope.

findings.title: Replicated broker and durable queues cover the core reliability path
findings.explanation: The design consistently routes publishes through a replicated broker, durable subscription backlogs, durable retry storage, and a dead-letter queue, which gives a coherent path for persistence, retries, and terminal failure handling.

findings.title: Priority and ordering are integrated into the work-queue model
findings.explanation: The point-to-point queue explicitly combines priority scheduling with FIFO ordering within each ordering key, which is a strong fit for the stated priority-queue constraint without sacrificing per-key ordering.

findings.title: Clear separation between search, inventory ownership, and payment handling

findings.title: Idempotency and transactional outbox improve retry safety

findings.title: Timezone-safe recurrence expansion is explicitly modeled

findings.title: Sync and notification paths are durable and revalidated

findings.title: Privacy-aware friend presence handling is built into the flow

findings.title: Rebuildable projections reduce coupling between canonical data and search

findings.title: High-volume count path is shard-aware and replayable
findings.explanation: Viral-post writes are distributed by shard, transitions are durable and uniquely identified, and the aggregation layer can rebuild from rollups and reconciliation. That is a strong fit for the stated scale and eventual-consistency model.

findings.explanation: Retry envelopes carry original IDs, sequence numbers, ordering keys, attempt history, and due times, and terminal failures are retained in a dead-letter queue. findings.title: Availability is advisory, but no enforced scheduling path is shown
findings.explanation: The design provides availability queries and overlap detection, yet the Availability + Conflict Service explicitly says free/busy is advisory unless a separate reservation transaction exists. No such reservation component or connection is defined, so the architecture does not clearly show how a client turns an availability result into a conflict-free scheduling decision for event creation.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit scheduling/reservation decision path in the Calendar API that checks current busy state and either commits the event atomically or returns a conflict when the slot is no longer available.

results.summary: The design covers experiment creation, deterministic assignment, event ingestion, statistical analysis, concurrent experiments, segmentation, gradual rollouts, and live monitoring with a coherent control-plane and data-plane split.

findings.title: Deterministic sticky assignment and durable ledgering support experiment correctness
findings.explanation: The design preserves first assignment per user and experiment, and persists the assignment with configuration version plus an outbox record. That combination supports consistent variant assignment and downstream correlation after retries or cache misses.

findings.title: End-to-end live monitoring is explicitly modeled
findings.explanation: The live monitor surfaces assignment errors, event freshness, processing lag, per-variant counts, and sample-ratio diagnostics, which is strong operational coverage for a testing platform.

results.summary: The design uses an authoritative membership store, asynchronous derived counters, reconciliation, and authorized live fan-out to cover real-time likes, unlike handling, duplicate prevention, and hot-post scaling.

findings.title: Sharded exact-membership and derived-count split is well aligned with hot-post scale
findings.explanation: The design cleanly separates authoritative membership from derived count projections, which is a strong fit for viral posts and high write volume while preserving recoverability.

findings.title: Real-time visible count updates are supported through cache plus fan-out
findings.explanation: The architecture provides both a fast read path for counts and a live update path for active viewers, so the UI can reflect changes without waiting for recomputation on every request.

results.summary: The design strongly covers nearby search, filters, reviews, mobile access, and consent-aware friend presence, with good use of geospatial indexing and cache/projection layers. Remaining gaps are mostly around explicit global-routing, failure fallback, operational visibility, and implementation-ready degraded-mode behavior.

findings.title: Global scale strategy is directionally sound but not fully specified
findings.explanation: The design shows geographic sharding, cross-region replication, and rebuildable projections, which are appropriate for millions of users and places. However, it does not spell out cross-region request routing or how query ownership is selected globally, so the scale story remains slightly underdefined for worldwide traffic distribution.
findings.recommendation: Add a brief global-routing strategy, such as region affinity with nearest-region reads and controlled replication/failover for writes.

findings.title: Failure handling for location freshness is partially implicit
findings.explanation: The architecture uses expiring presence, versioned updates, and idempotent consumers, which helps reliability. But the response path relies on freshness metadata and asynchronous projection updates without an explicit fallback for stale or missing presence state, so the user-visible behavior during propagation delays is not fully defined.
findings.recommendation: Specify the read-path fallback when presence or projection freshness is degraded, such as returning stale-labeled results, retrying from canonical state, or suppressing friend visibility until revalidated.

findings.title: Authorization model for friend presence could use tighter read-path detail
findings.explanation: The system includes JWT authentication, audience authorization, consent-version revocation, and opt-in gating, which is strong. The remaining ambiguity is the exact enforcement point for friend-result reads when cache or index entries are stale; that is a clarification issue rather than a missing control.
findings.recommendation: Clarify whether every friend-location read is reauthorized against canonical consent before returning cached or projected results.

findings.title: Query path is well-designed but exact latency behavior is unproven
findings.explanation: The design has the right performance primitives for low-latency geo queries: bounded candidate retrieval, cache-aside hot queries, and exact-distance verification outside the index. Still, the system does not specify cache hit expectations, index fanout bounds, or any load-shedding strategy for very hot regions, so performance under bursty demand remains partly unspecified.
findings.recommendation: Add a brief hot-path policy for cache use, candidate limits, and degradation behavior when the query rate spikes in a dense region.

findings.title: Operational visibility is present but not comprehensive
findings.explanation: The design exposes projection freshness metadata and consumer lag, which is a useful observability baseline. However, it does not explicitly surface request-level metrics or alerting hooks for stale presence, cache invalidation delays, or geo-index rebuild failure, leaving some important operational failure modes only partially observable.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit metrics/alerts for query latency, cache hit rate, presence staleness, index rebuild lag, and consumer failure rate.

findings.title: Implementation detail is sufficient, but a few policy choices remain open
findings.explanation: The design gives concrete roles, data flows, and update semantics, so it is implementable at a high level. The only open pieces are freshness windows and the exact cache invalidation policy, which are tractable product/operations decisions rather than blocking gaps.
findings.recommendation: Document the freshness policy and invalidation thresholds for cached place results and presence entries.

findings.title: Request routing and service responsibilities are clearly separated
findings.explanation: The gateway authenticates and validates, the backend applies query and consent logic, the index handles spatial retrieval, and workers handle refresh/projection. This separation makes the design easy to reason about and matches the mobile-first and geo-query scope well.

findings.title: Cost profile is reasonable but not explicitly bounded
findings.explanation: Using rebuildable projections, cache-aside hot queries, and bounded geospatial candidate retrieval is cost-conscious for a high-query-volume service. The remaining cost uncertainty is the operational expense of cross-region replication and dual storage of projections versus canonical data, which is not justified with workload assumptions.
findings.recommendation: State the intended read/write mix or region footprint assumptions, and note which replicas or caches can be scaled down during low demand.

findings.title: Most core behaviors are covered, with one scope nuance around friend results
findings.explanation: The architecture addresses nearby place search, filters, reviews, mobile access, and real-time updates. The friend-presence path is present, but its read-time policy depends on freshness and authorization checks that are split across layers, so the core behavior is covered with some operational nuance.
findings.recommendation: Keep the friend-results path explicitly documented as a consent-checked, freshness-labeled read flow.

findings.title: Constraint compliance is strong, but global scale could be stated more concretely
findings.explanation: The design meets the key constraints with geospatial indexing, low-latency query paths, and frequent-update handling. The only remaining issue is that global scale is implied through geographic sharding and cross-region replication rather than fully spelled out as an end-to-end traffic placement strategy.
findings.recommendation: Describe the region-selection policy for reads and how writes or updates propagate between regions.

findings.title: Component responsibilities are coherent and well-justified
findings.explanation: Each major component has a clear purpose: mobile client, gateway, backend service, canonical store, search index, cache, broker, and workers. The indexing and cache choices are particularly well aligned with the location-query workload and update patterns.

findings.title: Connection semantics are mostly clear but hot-path degradation is not described
findings.explanation: The connections include direction, protocol, and purpose, which makes the data flow understandable. What is still unclear is how the service behaves if the geospatial index, event stream, or cache is temporarily unavailable during a query burst.
findings.recommendation: Add fallback behavior for index/cache unavailability, such as degraded results, retries, or temporary suppression of friend presence reads.

findings.title: Implementation handoff details are sufficient for core flows
findings.explanation: The architecture includes concrete components, data stores, projections, and message flow for the core feature set, so a team could start implementation from it. It still needs explicit policy decisions for freshness and regional routing, but those are refinement items rather than blockers.

findings.title: Missing explicit implementation readiness for query-response degradation
findings.explanation: The design does not specify the exact API behavior when the geo index or cache is partially unavailable, which affects whether the system can be handed off without ambiguity for the hot query path.
findings.recommendation: Document whether the service should fail open with stale data, fail closed, or return partial results under component degradation.

results.summary: The architecture covers login, registration, password hashing, sessions, MFA, reset, OAuth/social login, rate limiting, and scale-out handling well; the main unresolved core issue is that GDPR/privacy compliance is acknowledged but not fully demonstrated.

findings.title: GDPR compliance is not fully demonstrated
findings.explanation: The storage components intentionally minimize data and define review-based retention, but the design stops short of showing concrete GDPR controls such as lawful-basis handling, data-subject workflow implementation, or a complete privacy compliance path. Because the brief explicitly includes GDPR and privacy compliance, this remains a core constraint gap rather than a mere optional enhancement.
findings.recommendation: Add the specific GDPR/privacy controls you intend to operationalize, such as data-subject request handling, retention/deletion workflow ownership, and the enforcement points for lawful processing and auditability.

findings.title: Opaque server-side sessions are a strong fit for revocation-heavy authentication
findings.explanation: The design’s choice of Redis-resolved opaque sessions supports logout, password reset, MFA recovery, and other security-driven revocation without waiting for token expiry, which is well matched to the stated authentication scope.

findings.title: Rate limiting is distributed and abuse-aware
findings.explanation: The limiter shares per-IP and per-account counters across instances and avoids revealing account existence, which directly supports brute-force resistance at the edge of the authentication flow.
